Article Title: 'Saddened by the news': Stalin mourns VS Babu, who unseated him in Kolathur
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former Tamil Nadu chief minister and DMK chief MK Stalin on Thursday condoled the death of TVK MLA VS Babu following a cardiac arrest.In a social media post on X, Stalin said that the news of the TVK MLA's passing came as a shock to him."I am saddened by the news of the passing of Mr VS Babu, member of the legislative assembly for the Kolathur constituency. Reports had continued to indicate that his condition was improving after many days of treatment in hospital, so the sudden news of his passing comes as a shock," Stalin said."I extend my deepest condolences and sympathy to his bereaved family and to the members of his party," he added.The 75-year-old Babu was admitted to MGM Healthcare here on September 9 with a prolonged respiratory illness and remained under intensive care."Despite comprehensive medical management and the best efforts of our multidisciplinary clinical team, his condition continued to deteriorate. He subsequently suffered a cardiac arrest and passed away at 2.24 pm on Thursday," Rajesh Agarwal, director - medical services, said in an official statement.Earlier in May, Babu had caused perhaps the biggest political shock of the Tamil Nadu assembly elections by defeating DMK chief MK Stalin.Babu defeated Stalin in Kolathur by 8,795 votes. Stalin had represented the constituency since 2011.Babu represented Purasawalkam in the assembly from 2006 to 2011 after winning on a DMK ticket.He joined the AIADMK in June 2016 before moving to TVK on February 7, 2026. The party subsequently fielded him against Stalin in Kolathur.
Article Summary: TVK MLA VS Babu died on Thursday following a cardiac arrest. The 75-year-old was admitted to MGM Healthcare here on September 9 with a prolonged respiratory illness. Babu had caused perhaps the biggest political shock of the Tamil Nadu assembly elections by defeating DMK chief MK Stalin.

Article Title: US court to Delhi courts: Help serve summons to R&AW ex-chief, Doval
Article Text:
NSA Ajit Doval (File photo)

US court move a 'procedural, routine' step

NEW DELHI: A US district court has ordered alternative delivery of summons through Indian courts on NSA Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing chief Samant Goel. However, sources said the summons was not binding.The Clerk of the US Court has been directed to send the necessary judicial documents via international mail or courier to three district courts in Delhi - Patiala House, Dwarka and Tis Hazari district courts.The order was issued by Judge Katherine Polk Failla of the court of Southern District of New York in a civil lawsuit filed by Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, founder of pro-Khalistan outfit Sikhs for Justice (SFJ).“The court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court,” says an order by a US district court, seeking to serve summons on Ajit Doval and Samant Goel.The order states that standard service through India's central authority under the Hague Convention was attempted but rejected. The court then authorised alternative service under Article 19 of the Hague Convention and India's Code of Civil Procedure.Sources described the move as a “routine, procedural step”. Earlier, the summons was delivered through the Indian embassy by the US State Department, which had clarified that this did not reflect any position on the case.In 2013, former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh was served with a civil summons in a suit filed by SFJ, alleging human rights violations related to the 1984 riots.
Article Summary: US court move a 'procedural, routine' step, sources say. Move follows a civil lawsuit filed by Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, founder of pro-Khalistan outfit Sikhs for Justice. In 2013, former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh was served with a civil summons in a suit filed by SFJ.

Article Title: Can an Italian raise slogans against govt while in India on visa? SC to hear PIL
Article Text:
Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck

Telangana govt organised meet, examine its role: Petitioner

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday agreed to hear a PIL asking whether it was legally permissible for an Italian visiting India on a conference visa, to raise the political slogan "vote chor, gaddi chhod" in support of opposition's campaign against Election Commission and Modi govt at the Bharat Summit organised by Telangana Congress govt in Hyderabad.The plea alleges Giacomo Filibeck, the secretary-general of the Party of European Socialists, raised the "vulgar, derogatory and demeaning political slogan" and translated it for other foreign delegates as "vote thief, leave from seat."Senior advocate Rizwan Ahmad sought an urgent hearing on the petition filed by Zahid Ali.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana agreed to list the petition before a bench Friday.Ahmad informed the court that Filibeck, endorsing the leader of the opposition’s campaign, told the audience that the largest democracy in India had become corrupted and declared that “we stand by Rahul Gandhi, the Indian Congress party in defending the democracy in India”.Ahmad said the petitioner did not question Indian politicians criticising govt but “the endorsement and amplification of such domestic political positions by foreign political representatives, who are themselves associated with political organisations in other countries, raises a distinct concern regarding foreign participation in India’s internal political discourse, particularly when such participation extends to the endorsement of controversial domestic political positions...”The petitioner said when home ministry rules prohibited foreign delegates from taking part in any activity beyond the purpose of their visit to India, it was necessary for the court to examine whether Filibeck conformed to the visa conditions by getting involved in the political activities espoused by the opposition.He sought judicial scrutiny of Filibeck’s conduct and requested the court to direct Union govt to take action. “The role of Telangana govt also warrants consideration, particularly as the conference was organised by the state govt and provided a platform for the aforesaid political discourse involving foreigners,” he said.The petitioner also requested SC to direct social media platforms to take down videos of the conference relating to the Italian’s remarks.
Article Summary: The plea alleges Giacomo Filibeck raised the "vulgar, derogatory and demeaning political slogan" and translated it for other foreign delegates as "vote thief, leave from seat" Senior advocate Rizwan Ahmad sought an urgent hearing on the petition filed by Zahid Ali.

Article Title: 'Families of ministers, officials': BJP alleges AAP links in Punjab PSC selections
Article Text:
BJP accuses Mann govt of fraud in PPSC recruitment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Thursday accused the ruling Aam Aadmi Party government in Punjab of favouritism and irregularities in the Punjab Public Service Commission (PPSC) recruitment process. The BJP alleged that several candidates shortlisted for government jobs had links to the Kejriwal-led party and its leaders.Addressing a presser in Delhi, BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi questioned the selection of candidates, with the results announced on November 4."There are four categories," Trivedi said, alleging that some shortlisted candidates were related to political leaders and ministers, while others had family connections with officials considered close to the state government.He elaborated on 'four categories' saying, "one consists of people connected to the families of leaders and ministers; the second consists of people connected to the families of officials considered very close to this so-called staunchly honest government; and the third consists of people connected to the families of those facing corruption charges. The fourth category consists of people who have offered some floral tributes to the Aam Aadmi Party, directly or indirectly. "Raising questions over the examination pattern, BJP leader said reports that 24% of candidates from a single centre had cleared the examination were suspicious."This in itself raises suspicion," he said, adding that the selection of candidates in different rooms at four examination centres also raised doubts about the process.The allegations come days after several candidates who appeared for the Punjab Civil Services (PCS) and Allied Services examination approached the Punjab and Haryana high court, alleging large-scale irregularities in the selection process.The petitioners have sought a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the recruitment process, raising questions over the conduct of the examination and the selection of candidates.
Article Summary: BJP accuses ruling Aam Aadmi Party government in Punjab of favouritism and irregularities in the Punjab Public Service Commission (PPSC) recruitment process. Allegations come days after several candidates who appeared for the Punjab Civil Services (PCS) and Allied Services examination approached the Punjab and Haryana high court.

Azam Khan released from Ghaziabad jail (PTI)

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the Enforcement Directorate (ED) be scrutinized for its handling of the case against Azam Khan? Yes, they should be held accountable. LUCKNOW: Samajwadi Party veteran Azam Khan walked out of Ghaziabad's Dasna jail Wednesday, a day after the Allahabad high court granted him interim bail in the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University and Jauhar Trust case, holding that ED failed to supply written grounds of arrest when taking him into custody.Justices Rajiv Gupta and Devendra Singh gave ED a week to file a detailed reply and allowed Azam 10 days to submit his rejoinder. The next hearing is on Dec 10.On Wednesday, ED moved Supreme Court against the HC order, seeking an urgent hearing. However, Justice Joymalya Bagchi rejected the plea, saying, "The sky will not fall. Let him remain on interim bail." The matter is scheduled to be taken up on Friday.Azam, 78, had been lodged in jail since Nov 17 last year in a double PAN card case. Although he had briefly walked out of Rampur jail on Oct 31, he was immediately arrested by ED in the Jauhar University case. He was subsequently shifted to Dasna jail.ED has been examining alleged diversion and misuse of govt funds and construction material, land purchases and the sources of money used in developing the university. It has identified Rs 426.5 crore as alleged proceeds of crime and, on Oct 28, provisionally attached land and buildings belonging to the university valued at the same amount.More than 600 supporters gathered outside Dasna jail to welcome him. His sons, Abdullah Azam and Adeeb, received him, with the latter describing the occasion as Eid for the family. "Tiger is back," said Abdullah. Asked whether his father would contest the UP assembly elections, Adeeb said he would definitely enter the electoral fray.Azam left in a convoy for his hometown, Rampur, without making any statement outside the jail. Azam's wife Tazeen Fatima said she had faith in God and the judicial system. She alleged certain forces did not want her husband to be released and said the HC had once again delivered justice.Govt has done injustice to Azam, says Akhilesh: Welcoming his release from jail, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav alleged UP govt subjected Azam and his family to injustice over several years in false cases.
Article Summary: Azam Khan walked out of Ghaziabad's Dasna jail Wednesday. The Allahabad high court granted him interim bail in the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University case. He had been lodged in jail since Nov 17 last year in a double PAN card case.

NEW DELHI: Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh on Wednesday said the party is likely to release its first list of candidates for the upcoming assembly polls within the next 10-15 days.According to news agency PTI, Singh said the criteria for party tickets would not be limited to winnability alone, adding that candidates with a good public image, strong character and commitment to society should be given opportunities strictly on merit."Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has a clear vision that candidates with a clean image, strong character and commitment towards society should be given opportunities strictly on merit," Singh said."Congress had conducted more than 2,000 sample surveys, and the survey process was still under way," he added.Pargat Singh also appealed to party leaders and workers to enter the electoral battlefield with full strength and unity.He added that the atmosphere in Punjab was steadily turning in favour of the party.Addressing a workers' convention in Tarn Taran, Singh said that during the 2022 polls, the people of Punjab had given AAP an opportunity in the hope of change, but its MLAs had turned a deaf ear to public concerns."Instead of taking concrete decisions in the interest of Punjab over the past five years, the government had confined itself to posters, advertisements and misleading publicity. Today, Punjab is in the grip of lawlessness, with the law and order situation having completely deteriorated," Singh said.

Article Title: 'Suffering because of that': Moily says certain Congress leaders stalled probe against Modi during UPA regime
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Union minister and senior Congress leader M Veerappa Moily on Tuesday alleged that certain leaders within the grand-old-party had stalled the investigation against then Gujarat chief minister Narendra Modi during the UPA regime.While speaking at the launch of top Congress leader Sonia Gandhi 's memoir at the party headquarters at Bengaluru, Moily said that the decision led to political consequences for the party, news agency PTI said."We are suffering because of that today," he said.Recalling his tenure as Union law minister between 2009 and 2011, Moily referred to the investigation into the alleged fake encounter case of Sohrabuddin Sheikh, involving then Gujarat home minister Amit Shah."I was the law minister then. Amit Shah wouldn't have been the Union home minister today. He (Shah) was externed from Gujarat by the court. His case had to run in some other state. He was the first powerful leader to go to jail. Next would have been Modi to go inside (the jail) and he, too, would have been externed," Moily said, without getting into details."It wasn't because of (the then Prime Minister) Manmohan Singh. It was because of some other leaders.We are suffering because of that today," he added.The Congress leader also said that his party could have prevented Narendra Modi from coming to power as Prime Minister if certain party leaders had not resisted organisational reforms.Recalling Sonia Gandhi's efforts to bring "revolutionary changes" within the Congress, Moily said she had set up a committee under his chairmanship to examine how the party could prepare for future political challenges.Moily said Sonia Gandhi was keen to implement the committee's recommendations, but some party leaders resisted the proposed changes, citing difficulties in moving away from the existing arrangements."You know some of our leaders. They won't take even one step beyond the status quo. I don't want to name the leaders. They said the changes that were suggested were difficult to implement," he said, adding that the exercise eventually came to a halt due to these objections.Moily claimed that had the recommendations been implemented, Narendra Modi would not have come to power."If those changes were implemented, there was no question of Modi coming (to power) today," he said.The former Karnataka chief minister said the Congress should not shy away from taking bold decisions."We shouldn't be doubtful; being doubtful means allowing the enemy to come and finish you," he said.
Article Summary: Former Union minister M Veerappa Moily alleged that certain leaders within the grand-old-party had stalled the investigation against then Gujarat chief minister Narendra Modi. He was speaking at the launch of top Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir at the party headquarters at Bengaluru.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. NAVI MUMBAI: A 25-year-old woman on Monday lodged a rape complaint at CBD-Belapur police station against habitual offender Shailendra Dwivedi (50), who allegedly posed as a journalist.Dwivedi was arrested by Ulwe police on November 12 in a cheating and criminal breach of trust case for allegedly duping Thane trader Vijay Jha and four others of Rs 19 lakh in a flat sale deal. He is currently lodged in Taloja jail.Senior inspector Arun Pawar of CBD-Belapur police station said the woman alleged that on May 30 last year, she had attended a birthday party at Arush Hotel in Sector 15, CBD-Belapur, and was also there to collect Rs 10,000 from Jha. Dwivedi, who was present at the party, allegedly spiked her soft drink. After she felt dizzy, he took her to Arush Lodge and sexually assaulted her.She further alleged that Dwivedi threatened to kill her and her family if she disclosed the incident to anyone. He also threatened to circulate an intimate video, which he had allegedly recorded on his mobile phone.Pawar said, "The woman claimed that she did not approach the police earlier because of Dwivedi's threats.After learning that he had been arrested in another case and lodged in jail, she came forward and registered an FIR against him."Police have invoked relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to rape, administering stupefying or intoxicating substances, aggravated criminal intimidation and intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of public peace.(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme Court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A 25-year-old woman on Monday lodged a rape complaint at CBD-Belapur police station against habitual offender Shailendra Dwivedi (50), who allegedly posed as a journalist. Article Title: TVK MLA VS Babu, who defeated M K Stalin in Kolathur in 2026 assembly polls, dies after 71 days in hospital
Article Text:
Kolathur MLA V S Babu passed away due to a cardiac arrest after a lengthy illness

CHENNAI: Kolathur MLA V S Babu died following a cardiac arrest at MGM Healthcare on Thursday, more than 70 days after he was admitted with a respiratory illness.Babu had been under intensive care since his admission on September 9. “Despite comprehensive medical management and the best efforts of our multidisciplinary clinical team, his condition continued to deteriorate. He subsequently suffered a cardiac arrest and passed away on November 19 at 14:24 hours,” the hospital said in a statement.Babu defeated former chief minister M K Stalin in Kolathur by 8,795 votes in the 2026 Assembly election. Stalin had represented the constituency since 2011.Babu represented Purasawalkam in the Assembly from 2006 to 2011 after winning on a DMK ticket. He joined the AIADMK in June 2016 before moving to TVK on February 7, 2026. The party subsequently fielded him against Stalin in Kolathur.Babu was a councillor of the Greater Chennai Corporation for two terms from 1996. He was also the chairperson of the Ayanavaram Zone ward committee during M K Stalin’s tenure as mayor of the corporation between 1996-01.
Article Summary: Kolathur MLA V S Babu died following a cardiac arrest at MGM Healthcare on Thursday. Babu had been under intensive care since his admission on September 9. He defeated former chief minister M K Stalin in Kolathur by 8,795 votes in the 2026 Assembly election.

Article Title: Rash and wrong-side driving: Coimbatore district police book driver, seize private bus, recommend cancellation of licence and permit
Article Text:

COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore district police have seized a private mofussil bus and booked its driver for rash, negligent and wrong-side driving at Pappampatti Pirivu on the Coimbatore–Palladam Road.According to a statement issued by the district police on Tuesday, the incident occurred around 8.30am on Monday while the private bus was heading to Coimbatore from Tirupur. Near Pappampatti Pirivu, which falls under the Sulur police station limits, driver Sakthivel drove the bus at a high speed before abruptly swerving the vehicle to the right and driving against the oncoming traffic on the wrong side of the busy stretch, putting motorists and pedestrians at a grave risk.Several commuters recorded the dangerous manoeuvre and uploaded the footage online, where it quickly gained widespread traction. Acting on a formal complaint lodged by a motorist, the Sulur police registered a case against Sakthivel under Section 281 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) read with Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act Police impounded the bus and parked it on the Sulur police station premises for further legal proceedings. Additionally, authorities have written to the regional transport officer recommending the cancellation of Sakthivel’s driving licence as well as the vehicle’s route permit.Reiterating a zero-tolerance stance, the district police warned that strict legal action would be taken against motorists endangering public safety.
Article Summary: The Coimbatore district police seized a private mofussil bus and booked its driver for rash, negligent and wrong-side driving. Driver Sakthivel drove the bus at a high speed before abruptly swerving the vehicle to the right and driving against the oncoming traffic.

Article Title: Verdict on Sulur minor girl rape-murder case postponed to Nov 27
Article Text: COIMBATORE: A special court for Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act cases on Monday postponed to Nov 27 its verdict on the rape and murder of a 10-year-old girl near Sulur in Coimbatore district.The verdict was scheduled to be pronounced on Monday by judge Hariharan. No specific reason was stated for the postponement.On May 21, a 10-year-old girl from Pallapalayam near Sulur went missing after visiting a local shop. Her body was found the next day near the Kannampalayam lakebed. Police arrested K Karthi,35, and R Mohan, 31, both of whom were residing in the same locality.Police registered a case under sections 5(m), 5(i), 6(1), 5(I), 5(j)(iv), 16 and 17 of the POCSO Act and 103(1), 61(2)(a), 140(1), 140(4), 238(a), 127(2), 65, 49, 240, 249(a) of the BNS. The first hearing of the case took place on June 10. Prime accused Karthi was lodged in Madurai Central Prison, while Mohan was lodged in Trichy Central Prison.On Monday, both were produced before the court. While police were bringing them to the court, Mohan asked the media people not to take video of him, claiming that police had falsely included him in the case.
Article Summary: The verdict was scheduled to be pronounced on Monday by judge Hariharan. No specific reason was stated for the postponement. On May 21, a 10-year-old girl from Pallapalayam near Sulur went missing after visiting a local shop. Her body was found the next day near the Kannampalayan lakebed.

A man was arrested on Thursday for allegedly attacking a woman with scissors after she opposed his alleged pressure to convert and plan to marry another woman. The accused was arrested near COD bridge in Kanpur by Railbazar police.The woman, a resident of Kanpur, alleged in her complaint that the accused married her at a temple about five years ago and took her to Noida. She accused him of subsequently assaulting her and pressuring her to convert.She gave birth to a son in Sept. She alleged that the accused then called her back to Kanpur on the false assurance that he would perform nikah with her and accommodate her at his parents’ house. After arriving, she learnt that he was preparing to marry another woman.When she opposed the proposed marriage and refused to convert despite alleged pressure from Kaleem and his family, he attacked her neck with scissors with the intention of killing her, according to the complaint. He subsequently fled.Acting station house officer Ashish Chaubey said police registered a case under relevant sections based on the woman’s written complaint.During questioning, the accused admitted that he was attempting to flee to Noida.
